subject: Evangelion Pilot: Evaluation Charter & Stakeholder Lanes
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@evangelion.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Robin Yates <robin.y@evangelion.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evangelion pilot: evaluation charter & stakeholder lanes

Diego,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood's latency and quantization options. We're ready to kick off a short pilot but we'd like a concrete evaluation plan (MAP-style) that makes responsibilities and acceptance criteria clear.

Can you share a starter evaluation charter + stakeholder lanes we can co-edit? High-level asks from our side:
- Week0 owners and required accesses (we need to know infra/role access up front)
- Acceptance criteria for model quality (rough thresholds for precision/recall or label-based checks)
- Joint milestones (demo, perf check, cost run-rate estimate, acceptance)
- Procurement timeline: Robin will confirm PO timing but procurement@evangelion.ai is on copy.

If you can send a GDoc and a simple owners spreadsheet we can co-edit, that would help. Also open to a quick 30-min sync later this week to align stakeholders.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of AI Product
Evangelion AI
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@evangelion.ai>
Cc: Robin Yates <robin.y@evangelion.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 10:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evangelion pilot: evaluation charter & stakeholder lanes

Samira — great to hear. I pulled together a compact starter we use for 21–30d pilots. Attached: a GDoc scaffold (Evangelion-Eval-Template-v1.gdoc) and a Week0 owners spreadsheet (Week0-owners.xlsx). Quick notes:

- Proposed timeline: 30 days (Week0: infra & access; Week1–2: basic integration and perf baseline; Week3: stress/scale tests; Week4: acceptance review).
- Owners sheet maps Redwood contacts, Evangelion contacts, and primary deliverables per week.
- Acceptance criteria section includes both quantitative checks (tokens/latency/cost per 1k, top-1 accuracy on sample set) and qualitative gates (generated output safety review, hallucination spot-check).
- I added a "Risk & Mitigations" column to the template — callout for data egress and model quantization tradeoffs.

Can Marissa and Jasmine weigh in on the quantization profile recommendation and whether we should recommend a progressive rollout (float32 -> 8-bit quant -> 4-bit) during Week2?

If that looks good, I'll share the GDoc link and set a 30-min sync (proposed Thu 11/4 11:00 PT).

Attachments: Evangelion-Eval-Template-v1.gdoc (Google Doc stub), Week0-owners.xlsx

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@evangelion.ai>, Robin Yates <robin.y@evangelion.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 13:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evangelion pilot: evaluation charter & stakeholder lanes

Quick internal note (copying Samira/Robin for visibility):

Diego / Jasmine — I reviewed the starter doc. A couple of suggested additions before we share widely:
1) Add an "Operational SLOs" table for token latency p50/p95 and expected concurrency (helps sizing Dedicated vs hosted).
2) Include a short acceptance checklist for security/compliance (SOC 2 scope: logging, data retention expectations).
3) Add a small "rollback criteria" row so Evangelion has a clear opt-out path if perf or safety thresholds fail.

Diego — I'll drop a one-paragraph blurb for the quantization recommendation (what to expect quality-wise at 8-bit vs 4-bit) and attach to the doc. Jasmine, can you add a short test sample template for model-quality checks (labelled cases + golden answers)?

Marissa
Head of Customer Success (acting)
From: Samira Khan <samira@evangelion.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Robin Yates <robin.y@evangelion.ai>, procurement@evangelion.ai
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 11:45:00 -0500

Thanks — the template looks solid. Robin and I reviewed the owners sheet; procurement expects a PO by EOW (we'll confirm exact date). We're happy to co-edit the GDoc.

We can do Thu 11/4 14:00 ET / 11:00 PT for a 30-min sync to walk through acceptance criteria and owners (Robin will join). Can you send a calendar invite and a short agenda (10-min walkthrough, 10-min owners & access, 10-min next steps)?

Also, quick question on metrics: can you add a simple cost estimate row (approx tokens/hour and expected per-token cost for the proposed config) so procurement has something to look at?

Samira
